title: Experiment Comms & Ops Canvas (progressive rollout)
body:
Purpose:
This canvas captures a practical, comms-first ops play for progressive rollouts, with a focus on short micro-canaries for LLM-driven features (generation/chat/embedding routes). The goal is to align stakeholders, codify signals and actions, and provide message templates and technical gating details so teams can run low-friction, safe experiments across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.

Scope: 
- Applies to product feature launches and A/B experiments that change model variants, prompt templates, routing, or latency/cost controls.
- Excludes infra-only deploys (node upgrades, kernel changes) unless they affect model execution behavior.

High-level commitments (stakeholder matrix):
- Product owner: hypothesis, success metrics, rollout schedule, final go/no-go.
- Engineering (serving/runtime): implement route flags, fallback, and token-cost guard; own rollback commands.
- Observability: define dashboards, alerts, and tracing hooks for the experiment.
- SRE/Oncall: clearance to pause traffic, execute hotfixes, own incident comms channel.
- CS/Support: prepared support script and triage doc for customer queries.
- Legal/Privacy (if private deployments): confirm data retention and KMS constraints before canary.

Signal & gating rubric (stop/slow thresholds):
- Safety: any customer-facing hallucination regression flagged by QA or sampled user reports -> STOP and rollback.
- Reliability: 5xx rate increase > 2x baseline in a 10m window OR absolute 5xx > 0.5% -> PAUSE.
- Latency: P95 token latency increase > 2x baseline for > 5m -> SLOW (reduce batch size/route to cheaper variant).
- Cost: Spend burn rate for experiment traffic exceeds allocated budget by 30% in 1h -> PAUSE.
- Quality: Eval prompt A/B score delta (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) drops > 5% over baseline on monitored prompt set -> PAUSE and triage.
- User signals: NPS/ctr/engagement delta beyond expected CI -> evaluate; if severe user impact -> PAUSE.

Traffic choreography (micro-pulse pattern):
- Pulse 0: 0.1% for 10m (sanity), automated smoke tests run.
- Pulse 1: 1% for 15m with expanded synthetic traffic and elevated sampling for manual checks.
- Pulse 2: 5% for 30m, run automated quality eval suite and start cost burn monitoring.
- Pulse 3: 20% for 1h if pulses 0-2 green. Monitor regressions and user metrics.
- Ramp: incremental steps of 10–20% up to target over multiple hours/days depending on metric stability.

Assignment strategy (A/B):
- Use deterministic hash on user-id or session-id at the edge to ensure sticky exposures.
- Ensure experiment cookie TTL equals planned exposure window; include route tags for tracing.

Instrumentation & telemetry checklist: 
- Route tag on every request: experiment_id, cohort, variant_key, rollout_wave.
- Trace ID propagation from frontend through gateway to model runtime and back.
- Sampling: store full request/response for 1:500 sampled requests and all failures.
- Quality eval ingestion: automated pipeline to score sampled outputs vs golden prompts; nightly baseline comparisons.

Operational controls (APIs & quick actions):
- /v1/rollouts/{id}/pause -> immediate stop distributing new traffic to variant.
- /v1/rollouts/{id}/scale?percent= -> adjust allocation to variant in real time.
- /v1/rollouts/{id}/fallback -> route to fallback model variant (e.g., quantized or older stable checkpoint).
- Emergency rollback CLI: rwdctl rollout rollback --id {id} --to-stable --no-wait (executes within 30s).
- Cost cap enforcement: enforce per-rollout hourly token spend ceiling; auto-pause on breach.

Comms & run-book templates (use these verbatim for clarity):
- Slack pre-rollout message (prod-rollouts):
  "Starting rollout {id} -> variant {v}. Pulse: 0.1% for 10m. Owners: @Sofia, @Ethan. Observability: dashboards X/Y, sampling enabled. If critical signal -> @sre oncall will pause. Linked ticket: JIRA-INC-3478."

- Slack pause notification (automated):
  "AUTO-PAUSE: rollout {id} paused at {timestamp}. Reason: {primary_signal}. Current allocation: {percent}. Next step: triage & decision window 30m. Owners: product/eng/obs."

- Stakeholder status ping cadence:
  - After Pulse 1: 30m async update in thread (pass/fail + key metrics snapshot).
  - After Pulse 2: 60m sync standup (15 min) if any warning signals.
  - Pre-ramp to 20%: cross-functional sign-off (product + eng + obs).

Fallback map (model variants):
- Variant A (canary) -> Variant B (fallback: cheaper quantized) -> Variant C (stable with previous prompt template).
- Fallback triggers: latency spike, 5xx burst, quality regression on golden set.

Quality monitoring specifics for LLM features: 
- Define a "canary eval set" of 200 prompts representative of high-risk user flows.
- Run micro-evals on sampled traffic every 15m (batch scoring). Use threshold-based alerts.
- Monitor semantic drift via embedding distance to baseline cluster; alert on mean distance > 0.12.

Cost governance:
- Pre-declare token budget per rollout wave and hourly burn limit.
- Prefer shorter pulses with narrower cohorts to detect runaway costs earlier.
- Instrument per-route token counters and expose to billing dashboard.

Customer impact & support playbook: 
- Support script snippet for CS: short explanation, known issue template, affected cohort guidance, mitigation (rollback information), escalation link.
- If impacted accounts exist (dedicated/private), notify account lead and provide timeline for remediation and logs export.

Privacy & compliance note: 
- For private deployments, confirm KMS and retention policy before exposure. If PII-sensitive prompts are included in eval set, redact before storage.

Post-rollout retrospective triggers:
- Any auto-pause or rollback -> mandatory incident retro with timeline and RCA within 48h.
- If rollout increases cost per unit by > 15% without commensurate quality gains -> cost-performance review and possible revert.

Open questions & unresolved decisions (action owners):
- How long should we keep full request/response logs for sampled fails in hosted vs private? (Owner: Priya)
- Default cost buffer for new features: 20% or 30%? (Owner: Finance lead - Marcus)
- Should we default to model-fallback or region-fallback first on latency spikes? (Owner: Runtime lead - Ethan)

Action items (next steps):
- Engineering: add rollout route tags and implement /v1/rollouts auto-pause hooks (ETA 2w) -> Owner: Marcus Li.
- Observability: create the canary eval dashboard and wire alerts for semantic drift (ETA 1w) -> Owner: Janelle Ortiz.
- Product: finalize canary eval prompt set and tag critical user cohorts (ETA 3 days) -> Owner: Sofia Alvarez.
- Legal/Privacy: confirm retention limits and KMS constraints for private customers included in experiments (ETA 1w) -> Owner: Priya Natarajan.

Notes & rationale: 
- We prefer multiple short pulses rather than one long slow ramp because LLM regressions often appear as sudden quality anomalies or cost spikes tied to specific input distributions. Short pulses with high sampling give faster feedback with lower blast radius.
- Emphasize comms-first: many past friction points have been lack of clear ownership when a rollback happens. The one-line Slack message template and explicit owner list should eliminate ambiguity.

Appendix: quick-check checklist before starting pulse 0: 
- [ ] Rollout ticket created and linked to PRs and dashboards.
- [ ] Owners and oncall notified in slack thread.
- [ ] Canary eval prompt set uploaded and baseline scores visible.
- [ ] Token budget configured for rollout id.
- [ ] Fallback map configured in routing rules.
- [ ] Tracing and sampling enabled for experiment traffic.
